ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all UBOs, directors, shareholders, and authorized signatories against: (i) Samoa FIU domestic sanctions and PEP lists; (ii) OFAC Specially Designated Nationals (SDN) list; (iii) United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) FATF public statements and lists of jurisdictions under increased monitoring; (v) relevant Commonwealth and EU sanctions lists. Enhanced due diligence required where any individual is a PEP, family member or close associate of a PEP, or where any jurisdictional red flags arise. Ongoing transaction monitoring applies; adverse media checks and source-of-funds evidence required for all beneficial owners holding 25% or more.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA) Company Registry online name reservation and registration portal (operated in conjunction with the Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour for domestic companies; SIFA is the competent authority for International Companies)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Names of International Companies may be in English or any other language but must be expressed in Roman letters (Latin script) or in a transliterated Roman-letter form acceptable to the Registrar; Chinese-character-only names are not accepted; a name must include a required suffix or designation such as 'Limited', 'Ltd', 'Corporation', 'Inc', 'Pty Ltd', or equivalent indicating limited liability; names that are misleadingly similar to an existing registered name, names that imply a connection with the Government of Samoa or any government, and obscene or offensive names are prohibited.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant or authorized Samoa-licensed registered agent must submit a written appeal to the Registrar of International Companies through SIFA within 14 days of the rejection notice, stating the grounds for review, attaching the original name reservation reference and supporting evidence (consents from any relevant authority or disclaimers); the Registrar must decide within 7 business days; if refused, the applicant may request a reserved alternative name or challenge the decision through judicial review in the Supreme Court of Samoa. Reservation extensions may be requested in writing by the registered agent before expiry; a further fee applies and the Registrar may grant up to two extensions of 30 days each.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible within statutory limits. An International Company must maintain a registered office in Samoa at the address of its licensed registered agent; the physical presence of staff is not required for a pure kitting/3PL holding or administrative company. However, if the entity performs actual fulfillment, kitting, or assembly activities in Samoa, a physical licensed premises with appropriate zoning and business license may be required. Virtual office services provided by a licensed registered agent satisfy the registered-office obligation only for non-resident companies without actual business premises in Samoa.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to Moderate (analytical estimate: 15% probability in the first 12 months for a low-risk, non-resident International Company with no physical activity in Samoa; probability rises to 65% if the company later carries on physical kitting/assembly activities in Samoa and requires a local business license, customs bond, or labor registration).

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: International Companies Act 1987 (Samoa), as amended; Sections 5 (incorporation by registration), 7 (memorandum and articles), 8 (name restrictions), 9 (restrictions on carrying on domestic business), 30-33 (registered office and registered agent).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), Corporate Registry Division, Apia, Samoa.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Application for Incorporation of an International Company (Form ICA-1) together with executed Memorandum and Articles of Association.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; the International Companies Act 1987 dispenses with capital adequacy and escrow requirements. Shares may be issued at par value, in any currency, and partly paid unless the Articles provide otherwise.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: (1) That the Memorandum and Articles of Association subscribed and filed with the Samoa International Finance Authority are adopted in full. (2) That the subscribers to the Application for Incorporation subscribe to the initial ordinary shares allotted to them, as entered in the register of members. (3) That the registered office be established at the office of the licensed registered agent in Apia, Samoa. (4) That [Director Name] be appointed first director and [Officer Name] company secretary, each to serve until the first annual general meeting. (5) That the director be authorised to open settlement bank accounts, appoint payment-rail providers, and execute all ancillary documentation to obtain the Certificate of Incorporation and applicable operational approvals.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name Reservation and Licensed Registered Agent Engagement
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA Corporate Registry via a SIFA-licensed registered agent
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Instruct the licensed agent to submit a name reservation request to SIFA with up to two proposed company names, one of which includes a permissible suffix ('Limited', 'International Company', or abbreviations). Obtain the agent's signed consent to act as registered agent and registered office provider.
required_dossiers: Engagement letter with licensed registered agent
Passport copy of ultimate beneficial owner/incorporator
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is rejected as undesirable or confusingly similar, file an alternative name within 5 business days; the reservation is renewable.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Constitutional Documents
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Memorandum and Articles of Association consistent with the Third Schedule of the International Companies Act 1987, including object clauses covering warehousing, kitting, assembly, packaging, and logistics; specify share structure and director provisions. Execute by the subscriber and initial director.
required_dossiers: Consent to act as director (Form ICA-6)
Consent to act as secretary (if appointed)
Subscriber particulars and share subscription schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Amend defective clauses and re-execute; SIFA requisitions are addressed via the registered agent within 7 days of notification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Submission of Incorporation Application to SIFA
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the completed Form ICA-1 with the executed Memorandum and Articles, consents, and registered agent certificate. Pay the USD 100 government filing fee plus agent disbursements. SIFA examines compliance with the International Companies Act 1987 and issues the Certificate of Incorporation upon approval.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: Respond in writing to SIFA requisitions within 14 days; rectify omissions or amend the Articles; resubmit with corrected schedules without a fresh incorporation file number.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation and Post-Registration Endorsements
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upon approval, collect the Certificate of Incorporation and the certificate of registered office. Verify the legal name, company number, and date of incorporation. SIFA will note the company in its register and, where applicable, provide a certified copy for bank onboarding.
required_dossiers: Certified copy of the Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the certificate contains errors, apply to SIFA for rectification under section 13 of the International Companies Act 1987; the registry will reissue a corrected certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: First Board Meeting, Share Allotment, and Banking Onboarding
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors / commercial banks and payment-rail providers
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Hold the first board meeting or pass written resolutions (Unanimous Written Consent) to ratify the board resolution, allot subscriber shares, issue share certificates, adopt the company seal, and approve opening of bank accounts. Liaise with onboarding teams for ACH and Airwallex payment rails, submitting the certified incorporation dossier and economic substance self-declaration.
required_dossiers: First board resolution and share certificates
Director and beneficial owner passport copies and proof of address
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank or payment-rail provider queries KYC/AML documents, supplement with bank reference letters, notarised directors' resolutions, or corporate registry good-standing certificates and resubmit.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Commencement of Operations and Annual Compliance Setup
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: SIFA and Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour (MCIL)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Execute the operational lease or service contract for the fulfilment/kitting facility, demonstrate that the Company will not carry on domestic business with Samoan residents without a licence under section 9 of the Act, and calendarise the annual government fee and annual return filing. Maintain the register of members, directors, and charges at the registered office.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a domestic-business breach is alleged, suspend local contracting, apply to the Minister for a licence under section 9, or relocate physical operations to an offshore service provider; late annual fees are cured by payment with penalties.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Planning and Urban Management Authority (PUMA) under the Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), in coordination with the Samoa International Finance Authority for offshore-entity operating exemptions.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Development Consent / Building Occupancy Certificate for Light Warehousing and Fulfilment Operations (Planning and Urban Management Act 2004)

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministry of Natural Resources and Environment (MNRE), Samoa
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Category 2 - Registration (low-impact development): warehousing and light kitting/assembly operations not involving hazardous chemicals qualify for a simplified environmental registration with an Environmental Management Plan; a full EIA Report is not required unless the facility exceeds 2,000 m² or emits significant fumes.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Wastewater: no untreated discharge to groundwater; trade waste must meet Samoan effluent standards (pH 6-9, BOD < 50 mg/L, TSS < 50 mg/L) or be routed to an approved municipal system. VOC/air: solvent-based adhesives and coatings must be controlled to workplace exposure limits adopted under the Occupational Safety and Health Act 2002; volatile organic compound emissions below 0.5 kg/hour require only periodic ambient monitoring. Solid waste: segregation and disposal at the Tafaigata landfill under MNRE waste regulations; packaging waste must be recycled or exported where feasible.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certificate from the Samoa Fire and Emergency Services Authority (SFESA) confirming compliance with the National Building Code of Samoa (fire exits, extinguishers, alarms); structural load inspection certificate for racking and mezzanine systems; occupational clearance from MCIL under the Labour and Employment Relations Act 2013 and the Accident Compensation Act 1984 covering worksite registration, first-aid provisions, and employee safety induction for forklift and packaging machinery operations.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Ministry for Revenue of Samoa, Apia; official portal: https://www.revenue.gov.ws
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Samoa International Company (IC) is formed under the International Companies Act 1987 through a licensed registered agent. As a tax-exempt offshore entity, the IC does not obtain a domestic income-tax TIN or file income tax returns. If a TIN or GST identifier is required for customs, banking, or counterparty compliance, the registered agent submits a Samoa Taxpayer Registration application to the Ministry for Revenue, attaching certificate of incorporation, IC license, memorandum and articles of association, registered office address, beneficial ownership declarations, and passport copies of officers/shareholders. The IC must declare that it does not receive Samoa-source income and does not make taxable supplies in Samoa. Approval is administrative and typically granted within 5-7 business days.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Samoa has no check-the-box or U.S.-style entity classification election. A Samoa International Company cannot elect to become a taxable entity while remaining an IC. The only available mechanism is to revoke the IC status and re-domesticate as a Samoa company under the Companies Act 2006, which makes the entity subject to the 25% domestic corporate income tax rate and all Samoa taxation and anti-avoidance rules. No hybrid-mismatch election is available to an IC.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax - Samoa Goods and Services Tax (GST)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: WST 20,000 annual taxable turnover in Samoa; a tax-exempt International Company performing offshore fulfillment, kitting, assembly and logistics services for non-Samoa customers is not subject to GST registration unless it imports goods into Samoa or supplies goods/services to Samoa customers.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Samoa does not currently impose mandatory real-time fiscal clearance, continuous transaction controls, API-based e-invoicing, or digital stamping on ordinary commercial invoices. GST compliance is enforced through periodic GST returns, customs declarations, bank statements, and audit examinations. Where physical goods cross the Samoan border, the Samoa Customs Single Window/ASYCUDA World system captures import and export declarations for duty and GST purposes.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: A GST-registered supplier may apply the 0% rate for goods physically exported from Samoa, for international transport, and for certain offshore services performed wholly outside Samoa, provided the supplier retains transport and remittance evidence proving the goods/services left Samoa. For the tax-exempt International Company in this scope, offshore kitting and fulfillment outputs are outside the Samoan GST base entirely, which is equivalent to zero-rating without the compliance burden of GST registration or refund filing.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Misuse of export zero-rating or submission of false export documentation is treated as GST evasion or tax fraud. Penalties include 150% of the tax shortfall, monthly late-payment interest, fines up to WST 20,000, imprisonment up to 2 years, and retrospective GST reassessment at the 15% headline rate for the full invoice value. For a tax-exempt International Company, engaging in Samoa-sourced trading activity or deriving income from Samoa residents can trigger loss of exempt status, retroactive corporate tax assessment at 25%, and additional penalties under the Tax Administration Act.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Central Bank of Samoa (CBS) — Faletupe Tutotonu o Samoa, established under the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984; the Monetary Board administers exchange control pursuant to the Exchange Control Act 1975 and the Exchange Control Regulations 1976. All WST-denominated and cross-border transactions through Samoa require intermediation by a CBS-licensed authorized dealer.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The Samoan Tala (WST) operates under a managed float with an administrative distinction between current and capital account transactions. Current account flows (trade settlements, service fees, and ordinary operating disbursements) are effectively convertible through authorized dealers upon submission of underlying invoices and contracts. Capital account flows (equity injections, intercompany loans, loan repayments, and liquidation distributions) require CBS approval or authorized-dealer certification with supporting board resolutions and audited financials. Profit remittances are permissible upon proof of tax clearance and audited accounts. An International Company (IC) under the International Companies Act 1987 may denominate contracts and maintain accounts in foreign currency, materially reducing WST conversion friction; however, any physical conversion into WST must transit a licensed bank and comply with CBS reporting thresholds.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Under the Exchange Control Regulations 1976, export proceeds must be repatriated to Samoa within 180 days of the date of shipment. For IC-designated foreign currency accounts, the mandatory conversion ratio into WST is zero, provided the authorized dealer files the prescribed exchange control declaration and the IC submits an annual foreign currency account recertification to CBS. Proceeds may be retained in the approved foreign currency account to fund operational disbursements, including supplier payments, subcontractor settlements, and intercompany treasury movements.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Bank of South Pacific (BSP) Samoa Limited
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Foreign Currency Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Samoa maintains no dedicated Electronic Money Institution (EMI) or neobank licensing category; non-bank payment service providers require CBS authorization under the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007 and the Central Bank of Samoa Act 1984. No international EMI, including Airwallex, currently holds a Samoan money transmission license. Offshore digital EMIs may be used as collection-side global accounts for USD, EUR, and AUD receivables and for vendor payments outside Samoa, but any physical remittance into or out of the Samoan banking channel must transit a licensed authorized dealer. The WS_IC should designate a Samoa-licensed commercial bank as the primary settlement and escrow account holder, with the Airwallex global account serving as an auxiliary receivable conduit subject to weekly sweeps.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical appearance of directors is not statutorily mandatory where the IC is represented by a licensed registered agent under the International Companies Act 1987. Remote onboarding is permissible using notarized and apostilled identification, professional reference letters, and CBS-compliant video identification interviews. Registered agents must certify incorporation documents, registers of directors and shareholders, and beneficial ownership declarations. Banks reserve the right to require an in-person meeting at the Samoa branch for the sole director or for any shareholder controlling 10% or more of the issued capital.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Nominee director or nominee shareholder structure obscuring the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO).
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Completed beneficial ownership register with onchain UBO chain to final natural persons; registered agent compliance certificate; signed nominee declaration disclaiming beneficial interest; passport, proof of address, and curriculum vitae for each UBO; independent Dow Jones or Refinitiv screening report.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Tax-exempt IC status combined with broad treasury wording triggering perceived shell risk.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: IC registration certificate evidencing ISIC 5210 kitting and 3PL business scope; executed warehousing and fulfillment service contracts; principal office lease in Samoa; three-year business plan with transaction-flow forecasting; registered agent substance letter confirming commercial presence and operational coverage.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Initial capital injection sourced from a non-bank or high-risk jurisdiction.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Six months of shareholder bank statements; certified source-of-wealth report covering sale of shares, accumulated earnings, or inheritance; remittance advice and contract matching the stated capital purpose; open-banking audit trail; written confirmation that no cash funding was used.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-velocity third-party payment flows from co-mingled 3PL receivables flagged by fund movement monitoring.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AML/CFT compliance manual for the WS_IC treasury function; whitelist of clients and suppliers with sanctions screening results; payment narrative codes assigned to each transaction leg; periodic external audit of the payment operational matrix; reconciliation policy covering Airwallex and ACH_Direct sweeps.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Politically Exposed Person (PEP) flags or negative media on foreign trading counterparties.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Independent enhanced due diligence report per counterparty; sanctions and PEP screening at onboarding plus ongoing monitoring; structure chart evidencing absence of PEP control; legal opinion confirming arms-length commercial purpose of the trade relationship.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Routing via SWIFT MT103 through a recognized correspondent of the Samoa-licensed bank (ANZ Australia, BSP Australia, or United States correspondent hub). Field 70 must carry the IC registration number, share subscription reference or loan agreement identifier, and the purpose narrative 'Capital injection — International Company (ISIC 5210)' or 'IC intercompany funding'. The authorized dealer will file the CBS exchange control declaration; for amounts exceeding USD 50,000 equivalent, board resolutions and final UBO certification must be pre-delivered to the receiving bank, and proceeds will be credited to the Capital Escrow Account pending matching of registration extracts and source-of-funds documentation.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Supplier and subcontractor payments settle via SWIFT MT103 with field 70 referencing the commercial invoice and kitting purchase order. Documentary credits use MT700 and standby guarantees use MT760, issued through the Samoa bank's trade finance desk with confirmation by ANZ or BSP correspondent banks in Australia or the United States. US-dollar clearing is effected via the bank's New York correspondent using CHIPS or Fedwire; Australian-dollar clearing runs through APAC direct entry rails. No local WST clearing is required where the WS_IC treasury is fully USD-denominated. ACH_Direct and Airwallex rails are permitted only for low-value receivables below USD 10,000 from North American customers and must be swept at least weekly into the primary operational account to maintain reconciliation integrity.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright WST/USD forward contracts with a CBS-licensed authorized dealer (tenor up to 12 months) for projected WST operating expenses
Overnight and term foreign currency deposits in USD, EUR, and AUD to achieve natural hedging of the multi-currency receivable portfolio
Cross-currency swap agreements with a licensed authorized dealer where the underlying exposure exceeds USD 1 million and CBS prior approval is obtained
No over-the-counter non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) are permissible in the domestic Samoan market, as NDF trading would bypass CBS exchange-control oversight

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual License Fee Payment (Good Standing Renewal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Samoa Registrar of International Companies (Ministry of Commerce, Industry and Labour)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Anniversary of incorporation; payment must be received on or before the company's anniversary date each year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: A late fee of 10% on the unpaid amount applies if payment is more than 30 days overdue; continued non-payment for six months permits the Registrar to strike the company off the International Companies Register.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: No statutory audit requirement for Samoa International Companies; mandatory independent audit is not triggered by revenue, assets, or shareholders. An audit may be required only if the company's articles so provide or a shareholder resolution requires it.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) as applied in Samoa, or an equivalent national standard, for the preparation of voluntary accounts; the International Companies Act does not mandate a specific framework for internal accounting records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: No annual UBO filing to the Registrar is required for an International Company. The registered agent must maintain current beneficial ownership records under Samoa's AML/CFT law. Any share transfer or change of beneficial ownership must be promptly recorded in the statutory registers; the agent must obtain and retain supporting evidence. No annual confirmation of shareholding transfers is filed with the Registrar.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500 - 900 per year (including registered agent and registered office services)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Not required by law; if voluntarily audited, USD 3,000 - 6,000 per audit

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 27% general corporate income tax rate (Income Tax Act 2016); 0% statutory rate for licensed International Companies under the International Companies Act 1987
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: International Companies are exempt from income tax, capital gains tax, and stamp duty for 20 years from incorporation (ICA 1987, s. 79). Qualifying export-oriented fulfillment and light-manufacturing operations may obtain a 5-year tax holiday under the Enterprises Incentives Act. No payroll tax or social security levy applies to international company employees.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Company Income Tax Return (Form IR-201) filed via the Samoa Inland Revenue Department (IRD) e-Services online portal
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Due no later than 6 months after the fiscal year-end; amended returns permitted within 4 years of the original due date

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Report only Samoa-sourced income unless the company is tax resident; International Companies declare nil taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Allowable deductions directly attributable to income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only expenses with a proven nexus to Samoa-source income are deductible; group charges must satisfy the arm's length standard.
For International Companies, enter nil and reference the ICA 1987 exemption.
International Companies compute zero; no foreign tax credit is required on exempt profits.
Tick the exemption box and attach the SIFA certificate of incorporation to support the 0% effective rate.
Loss history may be carried forward only where the trade continues; ownership changes may forfeit the carryforward.
Disclose all transactions with affiliates, including cost recharges for kitting, assembly, and logistics services; attach TP documentation if thresholds are met.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing incurs a penalty of 10% of the self-assessed tax (minimum WST 500); late payment interest accrues at 2% per month. Fraudulent or misleading returns attract a civil penalty of 100% of the tax shortfall and criminal prosecution.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: International Company Annual Return and Government Fee Filing (Samoa International Finance Authority – SIFA Registry)
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual return and government fee due no later than 31 March for calendar-year entities or 30 days after the incorporation anniversary; no profit-based tax computation is required

field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The licensed Samoa registered agent must co-sign; non-resident directors may remain offshore.
No minimum capital; declare issued shares to compute the flat annual government fee.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Directors, shareholders, and beneficial owner registry
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Beneficial ownership information must be kept at the registered agent in Samoa and be available to SIFA on demand.
Confirm whether a relevant activity (distribution and service centre, fulfilment, or logistics) is conducted in Samoa and detail premises, employees, and expenditure.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Failure to file by the due date triggers automatic strike-off after 90 days, a reinstatement fee, and a SIFA penalty of up to WST 10,000; the registered agent may also be fined for non-compliance.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory dividend withholding tax on distributions by resident companies (Income Tax Act 2016); 0% for distributions paid by an International Company, which are statutorily exempt from all Samoan withholding taxes
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke treaty relief, the beneficial owner must submit Form T-101 (Application for Treaty Relief) to the Samoa IRD, accompanied by (i) a Tax Residency Certificate (TRC) issued by the Samoa IRD upon endorsement by SIFA, (ii) certification of beneficial ownership of at least 10% of the share capital, and (iii) confirmation from the counterpart tax authority that the income is taxable in the residence state. The reduced rate applies only after the IRD issues a withholding exemption certificate to the paying party. Under the Samoa-China DTA, the dividend rate is limited to 5% where the beneficial owner holds at least 10% of the voting shares.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Interest: 15% statutory, 10% under the Samoa-China DTA. Royalties: 15% statutory, 10% under the Samoa-China DTA. Payments made by an International Company to non-residents for royalties or interest are exempt from WHT; payments by a taxable resident company remain subject to statutory rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Contemporaneous Local File is mandatory where aggregate related-party turnover equals or exceeds WST 1,000,000 or where total gross revenue equals or exceeds WST 5,000,000. A Master File is required for multinational groups with consolidated revenue of WST 50,000,000 or more. Documentation must be filed with the IRD within 30 days of an official request and must be prepared before the tax return is lodged.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: The Economic Substance (Amendment) Act 2019 and the Economic Substance Regulations 2019, administered by the Samoa International Finance Authority (SIFA), require International Companies carrying on relevant activities to demonstrate genuine economic presence in Samoa. Fulfillment, kitting, and third-party logistics assembly are classified as a 'Distribution and Service Centre' relevant activity. The company must satisfy the CIGA test: (i) management and control exercised in Samoa, (ii) full-time qualified employees physically present in Samoa, (iii) adequate operating expenditure incurred in Samoa, and (iv) physical premises leased or owned in Samoa. An annual Economic Substance Return (Form ESR-1) must be filed through the registered agent; failure to file results in automatic exchange of information with foreign tax authorities and enforcement action.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate under-declaration of Samoa-source income, concealment of assets, or submission of false documentation to obtain the international company tax exemption for a domestic trading business
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Civil penalty of 200% of the tax evaded plus interest at 2% per month; criminal conviction carries a fine of up to WST 200,000 and imprisonment of up to 7 years
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and beneficial owners are jointly and severally liable for civil restitution; the court may impose travel bans, freeze personal assets, and, upon fraud conviction, impose imprisonment. The corporate veil is pierced where the company is used as a mere facade for tax evasion.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Maintaining an International Company with no physical office, no local employees, no Samoan bank account, and no substance while generating distribution, kitting, or assembly income; failing to file the ESR-1 return
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: SIFA may impose a penalty of up to WST 250,000, strike off the company from the register, and compulsorily exchange all commercial and beneficial ownership information with foreign revenue authorities
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be disqualified from acting as officers of any Samoa company for up to 5 years, subjected to court-ordered travel restrictions, and held personally liable for unpaid penalties where they wilfully certified false substance declarations.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Artificial transfer of profits out of Samoa through non-arm's length management fees, excessive cost recharges, or mispriced intercompany kitting and fulfillment service charges with affiliates in low-tax jurisdictions
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Full transfer pricing adjustment to the arm's length price, a 50% substantial understatement penalty on the resulting tax shortfall, monthly interest at 2%, and, for repeat offenses, referral for criminal tax evasion prosecution
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign defective TP documentation or knowingly approve sham recharging arrangements face personal civil liability for the shortfall, disqualification orders, and criminal sanctions where fraud is proven.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing customer payments through ACH or Airwallex rails without customer due diligence, transaction monitoring, or reporting of suspicious transactions contrary to the Money Laundering Prevention Act 2007
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Corporate fines of up to WST 1,000,000, revocation of any financial services registration, asset forfeiture, and blacklisting by the Samoa Financial Intelligence Unit
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers may be imprisoned for up to 14 years; individual fines up to WST 100,000; directors may be disqualified from managing any entity in Samoa and are subject to preventive travel restraints pending investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Repeated failure to lodge the SIFA annual return, late payment of the annual government fee, or failure to maintain beneficial ownership records at the registered agent
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Compounding fines, automatic strike-off after 90 days of default, confiscation of the company's assets by the Registrar, and a minimum reinstatement fee of WST 1,000 plus all outstanding fees
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The registered agent may sue directors for reimbursement of penalties; directors remain personally liable for liabilities incurred after the date the company ceased to be in good standing, and may be prohibited from departing Samoa pending settlement.
